clue.text: Beast stalked regularly visited Sussex town

indicators.note: only some letters of the phrase are called on, at even intervals, taking every other one starting with the first

explanation.surface: A wild animal prowled about a south-coast town on its rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of BEASTSTALKED gives the town, site of the 1066 battle near Hastings in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Battle is a small town in East Sussex named after the Norman Conquest fight of 1066.

clue.text: Space for dancing bear to hold hands with maiden

indicators.note: the bear holds the hands, enclosing them

parts.note: Baloo is the bear in Kipling's The Jungle Book
L and R stand for left and right hands
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A dancing bear makes room to hold hands with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing bear' runs together in the surface, but 'dancing' belongs to the definition. A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large hall for formal dances, a room set aside for dancing.

clue.text: King, say, besieging city given earl's protection

indicators.note: given means added to, so the earl joins the end

parts.note: Tutankhamun, King Tut, was the boy king of Egypt

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'say' surrounds the city, laying siege to it

parts.note: e.g., for example, means say
LA is Los Angeles
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A king besieges a city, with an earl offering protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King, say' reads as one example of a ruler, but 'say' is a separate piece meaning 'for example', and it is that which besieges the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is guardianship or instruction, the protective care of a tutor or guardian.

clue.text: Sensational cover featuring high-class stripper's bottom

indicators.note: the cover features, includes, the other letters within it

parts.note: a lid is a cover
U means upper-class, the opposite of non-U

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the stripper, whose bottom is taken

explanation.surface: A shocking magazine cover features a stripper's posterior, a classy touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' reads as the stripper's backside; it means the final letter of 'stripper's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking and vivid in a way designed to excite, as in tabloid journalism.

clue.text: Nationalist involved in low ruse essentially traded exclusive rights

indicators.note: the abbreviation for nationalist is wrapped up inside the cow's sound, as if caught up in it

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: essentially points to the heart of the ruse word, and traded means its two central letters swap places

parts.note: a ruse is a ploy, a cunning trick

explanation.surface: A nationalist caught up in a shabby scheme sold off sole commercial rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the verb a cow does, not 'base'. In the ruse word the two middle letters, its essence, change places.
explanation.definitionFit: A monopoly is sole control of a market or trade, an exclusive privilege granted to one supplier.

clue.text: Best starts to opening round in The Open?

parts.note: to best someone is to outdo them

indicators.note: the starts, first letters, of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Golf: the top starts to the first round at the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's major championship; read literally, 'in the open' means outside, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor means taking place outside, in the open air, rather than in a building.

clue.text: Quiet period back on terra firma depresses child

indicators.note: pushes down on, so in this down clue the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: back on dry land means off the sea
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A slack spell back on dry land gets a child down.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-season is the time of year when business or sport is slack, a lull.

clue.text: Sloth's middle toe is, surprisingly, superfluous

indicators.note: the middle points to the central letter of the five-letter animal name

parts.note: the animal's name, the sloth, whose middle is taken

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: The middle toe of a sloth is, oddly, unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of SLOTH is O, followed by TOEIS rearranged as TIOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no practical purpose, redundant or unneeded.

clue.text: Turn up in nomad's tent for dairy produce

indicators.note: the reversed word goes in the tent

parts.note: a yurt is the round felt tent of Central Asian nomads

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Arrive at a nomad's tent to find dairy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads as arrive; split, 'Turn' is a go in a game and 'up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is a dairy product made by fermenting milk with bacteria.

clue.text: Trendy model ultimately abandoned endangered species

parts.note: hip means trendy

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped, ultimately meaning at the end

parts.note: to model is to pose

explanation.surface: A fashionable model finally left a creature in danger of extinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippopotamuses are listed as a vulnerable species threatened by poaching and habitat loss.

clue.text: One who imposes order on masses

definitions.text: One who imposes order on masses

parts.words: One who imposes order on masses
parts.note: sounds like a crowd-control officer, but the masses are church services and the order is the set form of worship

explanation.walkthrough: 'masses' suggests crowds of people; here it means the Catholic Mass, and 'order' is the order of service.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgist is an expert in or compiler of liturgy, the prescribed form of public worship.

clue.text: Nothing fine about grand affair

indicators.note: turned about, so nothing-plus-fine is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Nothing very refined about a lavish romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fling is a short, casual romantic relationship, an affair.

clue.text: Communist touring Italy left in a huff

indicators.note: the communist goes around the other letters, as a tourist goes round a country

parts.note: a Red is a communist
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A communist on a tour of Italy departed in a sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb about departing; it only supplies L.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means irritated or angered, the state of someone who is in a huff.

clue.text: Academic papers about Foreign Office backing US state

indicators.note: the newspapers word goes about, around, the reversed abbreviation

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, Britain's foreign ministry
OR is the postal abbreviation for Oregon

explanation.surface: Newspapers report the Foreign Office supporting an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' means the press collectively, not documents; 'backing' reverses the ministry's initials rather than meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor is a senior university teacher, the highest rank of academic.

clue.text: Pirate captain discovered text revealing climactic events

indicators.note: dis-covered, with its cover removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: Captain Henry Morgan was a notorious 17th-century Welsh pirate
SMS is a text message on a phone

explanation.surface: A buccaneer chief found a message disclosing the climax of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' reads as found, but splits as dis-covered: the captain's name loses its covering letters at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgasm is the peak of sexual excitement, so these are climaxes in a literal sense.

clue.text: German is taken in by Molly's revolutionary argument

indicators.note: the letters are taken inside the reversed name
a revolution turns something round, so the name is reversed

explanation.surface: A German is fooled by Molly's radical political case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reads as describing Molly's argument; it reverses MOLLYS to SYLLOM, with GIS going in before the last M.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllogism is a form of logical argument drawing a conclusion from two premises.

clue.text: Threat of disaster is known

indicators.note: the answer is made of, drawn from, letters within the following words

explanation.surface: A disaster is a known danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threat of disaster' looks like the definition; only 'Threat' is, with the answer straddling the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk is the possibility of harm or loss, a danger or hazard.

clue.text: Record agents breaking in exponent of 15s

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log

indicators.note: the agents break into the word, splitting it

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, its agents

explanation.surface: Records show agents breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 15 Down, syllogisms, the classic tools of logic.
explanation.definitionFit: A logician is a specialist in logic, someone who uses and expounds syllogisms.

clue.text: Mouth of lake originally inspired unfinished film about Norway

indicators.note: originally points to the first letters of the two words
the shortened film title goes about, around, the abbreviation
the film loses its final letter

parts.note: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 thriller
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A lakeside estuary inspired an incomplete film about Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' looks like a noun (the mouth of a lake), but it is the verb, to mime words. PSYCH wraps N.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-synch is to move the lips in time with recorded words or song without actually singing.

clue.text: Tree line crossed by tailless feline

indicators.note: the line passes through the middle of the cat, crossing it
the cat loses its last letter, its tail

parts.note: a puma is a big cat, a feline

explanation.surface: A tree is crossed by a line of cats without tails.
explanation.walkthrough: PUMA without its tail is PUM; L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum is a fruit tree as well as its fruit.

clue.text: Perceive what Americans do down Lovers Lane

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., to discern or see with difficulty

definitions.text: what Americans do down Lovers Lane

explanation.walkthrough: A lovers' lane is a secluded spot where couples park and canoodle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both discern something and, in US slang, engage in passionate kissing.

clue.text: Food from tin enraged lion

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: an enraged animal thrashes about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A meal taken from a tin has made a lion furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannoli are Sicilian pastry tubes filled with sweet ricotta, a food.

clue.text: Charlie arranged duel outside golf club

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside, around, the golf letter
arranged means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie set up a duel outside the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' reads as one phrase; the club is the definition, a weapon not a golf iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short thick stick used as a weapon, a club.

clue.text: Ravenous chinchilla finally leaves country

indicators.note: the letter leaves, departs from, the country's name

parts.note: Hungary is a country in central Europe

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter

explanation.surface: A starving chinchilla eventually leaves the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungry means wanting food, ravenous being an intense degree of it.

clue.text: A blackleg upset nursing union? You can count on it!

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the letter like a nurse holding a baby
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, the word read upwards

parts.note: a scab or blackleg is a strike-breaker

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker is upset to be caring for a trade union, a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can count on it' sounds like 'it is reliable'; literally, it is a counting frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on rods used for calculating, so one literally counts on it.

clue.text: Lone buck roaming Germany without obstruction

indicators.note: letters that roam wander from their places into a new order

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A solitary male deer wanders freely across Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Unblocked means clear, with nothing in the way, free of any obstacle.

clue.text: Vessels primarily serving pelvic region

indicators.note: primarily, at first, points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the hips are the pelvic region

explanation.surface: Boats mainly serving the area around the pelvis.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are large seagoing vessels, boats.

clue.text: Steps of area within prison

definitions.note: the definition is plural; a stair can mean a whole flight of steps

indicators.note: the area abbreviation goes inside the prison word

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Steps of a yard inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair, in older and Scottish usage, is a staircase, a set of steps.

clue.text: Universal measure adopted by soldier outfitting company

indicators.note: the soldier takes the other letters in, adopting them as a family takes in a child

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume

explanation.surface: A soldier took a universal measure of kit from a supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfitting' means supplying clothes: the definition is a fashion house.
explanation.definitionFit: Gucci is an Italian luxury fashion house, a firm that dresses its customers.

clue.text: Working hollow platitude into speech

indicators.note: the reduced word goes into the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

indicators.note: hollowed out, keeping only the outer letters of platitude

explanation.surface: A tired platitude is worked into a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' reads as an adjective for an empty platitude, but it strips the word to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Operation is the functioning of a machine or system, its working, as in 'in operation'.

clue.text: Park most eye suspiciously, including yours truly

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the setter's pronoun
something done suspiciously is shifty, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: yours truly is the setter, so I

explanation.surface: Visitors to a park eye it most warily, the setter included.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a national park in California, famous for its granite cliffs and waterfalls.

clue.text: Servant girl grabbing Romeo's tool

indicators.note: the girl takes hold of the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a wench is an old word for a servant girl
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A maid snatches the tool belonging to Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo's' looks possessive; it just supplies R and ''s' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a spanner, a hand tool for gripping and turning nuts.
